notes:
Summary: LumenForge is a global industrial manufacturer evaluating Redwood Private VPC for inference powering operator advisory chat and document search over engineering manuals. Primary drivers: data residency, auditable access logs for regulators, long-term retention for safety incidents, and tight KMS control (CMEK/HSM).

Key security/audit requirements (explicit):
- SIEM export: must be able to forward structured logs to Splunk (HTTPS event collector) and support syslog/CEF for QRadar. Customer will run collector in their VPC and expects push or remote-write.
- Log schema: JSON schema required, stable field set. Required fields listed by security: timestamp (ISO8601), request_id, tenant_id/customer_account, user_id (hashed), endpoint (model+route), model_version, prompt_token_count, response_token_count, total_latency_ms, inference_stage (cache_hit|compute), http_status, error_code, response_digest (sha256).
- Access logs: include both control-plane (auth events, role changes, config updates) and data-plane (request/response metadata, token counts). Must include S3/object access logs for artifacts.
- Retention: default retention for access logs 7 years for safety/regulatory audits; security wants configurable retention per-log-class (30 days for verbose debug, 1 year for standard telemetry, 7 years for audit trail).
- Integrity & tamper-evidence: prefer append-only immutable store with signed log bundles or integration with their log-integrity service.
- Redaction: need configurable redaction rules before logs leave the VPC (PII/PHI removal).
- KMS: customer requires CMEK integration + HSM-backed keys and key rotation policy. Logs that contain sensitive metadata must be encrypted with customer-managed keys at rest and in transit to SIEM.
